content: 1. In the study by Ivashchenko et al. (2021), the mortality rate among patients treated with favipiravir was 2 out of 40, compared to 0 out of 20 in the standard of care (SOC) group. The calculated risk ratio was 2.56 (95% CI: 0.13 to 50.95), but the result was not statistically significant. The risk of bias was assessed as low for most domains, except for selective reporting, which was unclear. 2. Lou et al. (2021) reported no mortality events in either the favipiravir or SOC groups. Consequently, the risk ratio could not be estimated. The risk of bias was low across all domains. 3. Udwadia et al. (2020) observed 0 deaths in the favipiravir group (n=73) and 1 death in the SOC group (n=75). The risk ratio was 0.34 (95% CI: 0.01 to 8.27), indicating no significant difference. The risk of bias was low in all domains. 4. For mechanical ventilation, Ivashchenko et al. (2021) reported 2 events in the favipiravir group (n=40) and 0 events in the SOC group (n=20). The risk ratio was 2.56 (95% CI: 0.13 to 50.95). Lou et al. (2021) reported no events in either group, and Udwadia et al. (2020) reported 7 events in both the favipiravir (n=72) and SOC (n=75) groups, with a risk ratio of 1.04 (95% CI: 0.38 to 2.82). No significant differences were observed. 5. Regarding hospital discharge, Ivashchenko et al. (2021) reported 30 discharges in the favipiravir group (n=40) compared to 17 in the SOC group (n=20), with a risk ratio of 0.88 (95% CI: 0.68 to 1.14). Udwadia et al. (2020) reported 70 discharges in the favipiravir group (n=72) and 68 in the SOC group (n=75), with a risk ratio of 1.07 (95% CI: 0.99 to 1.16). The overall effect showed no significant difference. 6. For ICU transfer, Ivashchenko et al. (2021) reported 2 events in the favipiravir group (n=40) and 0 in the SOC group (n=20), with a risk ratio of 2.56 (95% CI: 0.13 to 50.95). Lou et al. (2021) reported 2 events in the favipiravir group (n=9) and 0 in the SOC group (n=10), with a risk ratio of 5.50 (95% CI: 0.30 to 101.28). No significant differences were observed. 7. Serious adverse events (SAEs) were reported by Lou et al. (2021) with 4 events in the favipiravir group (n=9) and 4 in the SOC group (n=10), yielding a risk ratio of 1.11 (95% CI: 0.39 to 3.19). Udwadia et al. (2020) reported no SAEs in the favipiravir group (n=73) and 1 in the SOC group (n=75), with a risk ratio of 0.34 (95% CI: 0.01 to 8.27). No significant differences were found. 8. Time to clinical improvement was shorter in the favipiravir group in studies by Ivashchenko et al. (2021) and Udwadia et al. (2020). The mean difference was -2.00 days (95% CI: -3.00 to -0.99), favoring favipiravir. Lou et al. (2021) reported no significant difference. 9. For umifenovir, mortality rates were reported by AlaviDarazam et al. (2021), Khodashahi et al. (2020), and Li et al. (2020). The pooled risk ratio was 0.88 (95% CI: 0.52 to 1.48), indicating no significant difference between umifenovir and SOC. 10. Invasive mechanical ventilation was reported by AlaviDarazam et al. (2021), with 17 events in the umifenovir group (n=51) and 14 in the SOC group (n=50). The risk ratio was 1.19 (95% CI: 0.66 to 2.15), showing no significant difference. 11. Length of hospital stay was shorter in the SOC group in the study by Khodashahi et al. (2020), with a mean difference of -3.46 days (95% CI: -4.64 to -2.28). AlaviDarazam et al. (2021) reported a longer stay in the umifenovir group, with a mean difference of 2.00 days (95% CI: 0.56 to 3.44). The overall effect was -1.28 days (95% CI: -2.19 to -0.37), favoring SOC. 12. ICU transfer was significantly lower in the umifenovir group in the study by Khodashahi et al. (2020), with a risk ratio of 0.05 (95% CI: 0.00 to 0.88). 13. No SAEs were reported in the umifenovir or SOC groups in studies by AlaviDarazam et al. (2021) and Li et al. (2020). 14. Time to clinical improvement was longer in the umifenovir group in the study by AlaviDarazam et al. (2021), with a mean difference of 2.00 days (95% CI: 0.27 to 3.73). 15. For baloxavir marboxil, Lou et al. (2021) reported 1 event of invasive mechanical ventilation in the baloxavir group (n=10) and none in the SOC group (n=10), with a risk ratio of 3.00 (95% CI: 0.14 to 65.90). No significant difference was observed. 16. ICU transfer on day 14 was reported by Lou et al. (2021), with 1 event in the baloxavir group (n=10) and none in the SOC group (n=10). The risk ratio was 3.00 (95% CI: 0.14 to 65.90), showing no significant difference. 17. Time to clinical improvement was similar between the baloxavir and SOC groups in Lou et al. (2021), with a mean difference of -1.00 days (95% CI: -22.40 to 20.40). No significant difference was observed.
